newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mortgage-backeds stay afloat versus T-notes.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mortgage-backeds stay afloat versus T-notes.

text.p: U.S. mortgage-backed securities remained well-bid in a quiet Monday afternoon session despite some grumbling from market players that prices are "a bit rich," traders said.
"Overall, prices are on the expensive end of a five-basis-point range," one mortgage expert said.
But retail buyers were able to narrow spreads since mortgage bankers kept supply thin, he said.
"With little mortgage banker selling, a large customer can come in to buy mortgages ... and (spreads) are going to tighten even though mortgages are expensive," he said.
Earlier in the session, pass-through spreads were about two basis points wider to their Treasury counterparts. But light retail buying in mortgages closed the gap, one Ginnie trader in New York said.
"It's pretty surprising after the opening we had," he said. "We were a little wider this morning. There was some minor buying and now we are back in line."
By 1520 EDT/1920 GMT, pass-throughs were flat to 5/32 higher overall, while comparable Treasuries were up 5/32 to 9/32.
Specifically, Ginnie Mae 30-year 8.0 percent paper was up 4/32 at 100-24/32 bid, yielding 117 basis points over the five-year Treasury note.
Comparable Fannie Mae paper was up 3/32 at 100-24/32 bid, and Freddie Mac 8.0 percent coupons were 4/32 higher, at 101 even bid.
The five-year Treasury note was up 5/32 at 99-19/32 bid to yield 6.72 percent, and the 10-year Treasury note was up 9/32 to yield 6.86 percent.
